hook: The revolutionary who made Cuba a communist state and ruled it for half a century.

pages.x: Fidel Castro was born in 1926 at Birán, in eastern Cuba, the son of a rich sugar planter from Spain. He studied law in Havana, where he was a fiery student politician.

On 26 July 1953 he led about 130 rebels in an attack on an army barracks, against the dictator Batista. It failed. At his trial he declared that history would absolve him. He was jailed, then freed in 1955.

In 1956 he sailed from Mexico with 81 men, Che Guevara among them, crammed on a small yacht, the Granma. Most were killed or captured when they landed. A handful escaped into the Sierra Maestra mountains.
From the mountains his guerrilla army grew. On 1 January 1959 Batista fled, and Castro, aged 32, took power.
He took over American-owned land and businesses and allied with the Soviet Union. Opponents were jailed or shot, the press was silenced, and hundreds of thousands of Cubans fled to the United States.
In 1961 young volunteers spread across the countryside and taught almost every Cuban to read. His government also gave free health care to all, and sent Cuban doctors around the world.
The CIA tried again and again to kill him, with ideas such as an exploding cigar and a poisoned diving suit. His security chief claimed to have counted 638 plots. He survived them all.

He ruled through the Cuban Missile Crisis and the fall of the Soviet Union, which left Cuba poor, and outlasted ten American presidents. He handed power to his brother Raúl in 2008, and died in 2016, aged 90.
Castro made Cuba a communist state 150 km from the United States. Some admire its schools and health care; others condemn the jailing of his opponents. He ruled for almost 50 years.
